milestones.title: Guardrails: strict TS, lint rules, jest, invariant/Result, standards checker, npm run verify
milestones.note:
Covers plan M1.1–M1.7, using §4 "Standards enforcement" for the values. Pin tsx@4.23.15 and @types/node@26.6.3 as devDependencies. @types/node 26.6.3 is already in node_modules as a transitive dependency, so only package.json proves the install. Both tsconfig.json and scripts/tsconfig.json must resolve strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitReturns, noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters to true, and the scripts program must include scripts/check/standards.ts. eslint.config.js needs max-lines-per-function {max: 60}, no-empty, @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises and @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check at error, plus a src/domain no-restricted-imports that bans react, react-native, expo* and @/. It must also ignore .cache/, .expo/ and .claude/, because worktrees under .claude/ break typescript-eslint's projectService (roomsmith/eslint.config.js documents this). The gates rely on these contracts. src/lib/invariant.ts exports invariant and InvariantError, and src/lib/result.ts exports ok, err and isOk (gate 11 calls invariant(false) directly). The package.json jest block uses preset jest-expo/ios, with testMatch kept inside src/**/__tests__. Every node:test case in scripts/check/__tests__/standards.test.ts has its rule id in its own name or in its describe block's name: fn-length, assertions, marker, skipped-test, recursion (two cases: a self-call and a cross-file a<->b cycle), silent-catch and clean. `npx tsx scripts/check/standards.ts` run with no arguments scans the repo including src/app, exits non-zero, and prints the file path and rule id for each violation. Gate 20 proves this by writing an unasserted function to src/app/ratchet-probe-tmp.tsx for one run. Retrofit src/app/_layout.tsx and src/app/index.tsx with at least 2 invariant() calls each. npm run verify must chain tsc for the app, tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json, eslint --max-warnings 0, the standards checker, jest and node --test. Traps: the checker must follow its own rules. It must walk the AST with an explicit stack, because a recursive visit/forEachChild is the recursion it bans. It must read TODO markers from comments and skips from call expressions, so the fixture strings in its own test file don't trip the repo scan. It must also settle how anonymous test callbacks longer than 5 lines meet the 2-assertion rule. The gates call node_modules/.bin directly because under CI=1 a bare npx quietly downloads a missing tool. lib.sh's nodetest_nonempty is a false green on Node 26: the file-level wrapper counts as a pass, so an empty test file passes. That is why gates 12–19 count the real named passes themselves.

GATE NAMING (from the gate fix pass): Gates 13-19 count only passing test leaves whose full name 'describe … it' matches the keyword (fn-length, assertions, marker, skipped-test, recursion x2, silent-catch, clean). Put each keyword in the it() name, for example it('fn-length: flags a 61-line function'), and keep describe names free of those words, because a describe titled 'clean' or 'recursion' would make every test under it match. Gate 21 finds every .tsx under src/app and needs >= 2 standalone invariant( calls in each. Every route or layout component must therefore be a named function with its own invariants (no anonymous default-export arrow). The standards checker must print violations with a path that contains src/app/ (gate 20 needs 'ratchet-probe-tmp' and 'assertions' in its output) and exit 0 only when the whole repo is clean.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

milestones.title: Our own GTFS-realtime protobuf decoder, proven against the protobufjs oracle
milestones.note:
This card covers plan tasks M1.8–M1.13 (§5, plus the §4 "GTFS-RT decoder" bullet). The builder writes wire.ts, utf8.ts, decode-feed.ts, decode-vehicle.ts and decode-trip-update.ts as pure code under src/domain/gtfsrt, with tests in __tests__. It also runs `npm i -D gtfs-realtime-bindings@2.2.0`, which is the npm latest and depends on protobufjs ^8 and long. Then it writes scripts/fixtures/make-gtfsrt-fixture.ts, which generates __fixtures__/vehicle-positions.fixture.ts. The card depends on m1a_guardrails for jest, tsx and `npm run verify`.

TEST NAMES ARE GATED. Each pattern below is a case-insensitive regex matched against the describe+it full name, and it must match at least one PASSED test:
- wire: `300`, `negative`, `float32`, `wire type 3`, `past the end`
- utf8: one test per string, named with `Gov’t Center` (curly U+2019), `Ñ`, `🚆` and `abc`, plus a test named with `FFFD`
- decode-vehicle: `timestamp`, `latitude`, `trip id`, `unknown field 1000`
- decode-trip-update: `-45`, `arrival time`, `stopId`, `SKIPPED`
- oracle: `3 vehicles`, `2 trip updates`, `uint64`, `unicode`

Traps:
- Ten-byte -1 and delay -45 are sign-extended 10-byte varints, so they need int32 `|0` truncation. Do not use 32-bit `<<` past 28 bits.
- protobufjs decodes uint64 as a Long, so compare via `toObject(m, {longs: Number})`.
- No non-test file under src/ (the fixture included) may contain the quoted string 'protobufjs' or 'gtfs-realtime-bindings'. The src/domain no-restricted-imports rule must still allow the bindings inside __tests__.
- The generator must be deterministic: fixed timestamps, no Date.now and nothing that depends on the time zone. The gate deletes the fixture, regenerates it and requires it to match byte for byte. It then re-runs under TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati and runs `git diff --exit-code` against the index, so stage or commit a fixture that was changed after an earlier commit.

For the arbiter:
- lib.sh's `jest_nonempty <path> <name>` (the -t form) fails correct builds when a file has more than one test. Jest counts tests filtered out by -t as skipped, and the helper rejects any skipped test. That is why the card uses a local `jest_cases` (an unfiltered `--json` run) in its place.
- jest is not installed yet, so jest_cases' reading of the `--json` report (`testResults[].assertionResults[].{fullName,status}`) was proven only against shimmed reports. It has not been tested against a real jest binary.
- The verify runs about 10 jest passes plus full_gate.

Shared helpers: scripts/ratchet/lib.sh — nodetest_case matches the FULL test name (describe … leaf, case-insensitive), counts only real passing leaves (not parent test() wrappers, not the Node 26 empty-file wrapper) and forbids skip/todo; jest runs via node_modules/.bin only.

Five fixes, each proven by its OWN passing jest test whose full name ENDS with the quoted phrase (case-insensitive, at a word boundary; one test per phrase — a test ending with two card phrases counts for neither). REALTIME COST RULE: this card makes NO new live calls.
§1 MOVER FREEZE (gates 1, 3, 4). Root cause: reconcileLive.ts:66,72 clamps the projection at the next stop's arrival + 20 s (PROJECTION_GRACE_S); Mover trips have no dwell and stops ~60 s apart (trip 4829149: 0/0 s @499 m, 60/60 s @875 m), so the marker coasts 20 s past the station and freezes mid-track. FIX: a TIME-based clamp — the projection runs until the batch's fetchedAt + providerConfig(provider).cadenceS + 30 s (Transitland 90 s, Swiftly 60 s). Measure it from fetchedAt, NOT the fix's own timestamp: Transitland vehicles are already 35–155 s old when fetched (republish ~every 2 min), so a clamp from the fix time would re-freeze them. When it runs out, HOLD AT A STATION: the projection never ends mid-track — it stops at the last stop the timetable reaches at or before the clamp (or at the fix itself if none, never backward). New file src/ui/map/__tests__/vehicleMotion.test.ts, which value-imports AND calls planFrames and framesAt from src/ui/map/vehicleFrames (gate 3, a TypeScript-AST check: an `import type`, a mention, or a stub test that never runs them fails). The §1 cases use the REAL no-dwell Mover trip 4829149 from assets/db/schedule.db (arr = dep; from its start: 48 m @0 s, 499 m @60 s, 875 m @120 s, 1200 m @180 s, 1454 m @240 s — copy these public-schedule rows into the test fixture; schedule data, not a realtime capture). Gate 1 phrases: 'a mover keeps moving every second for 60 s between polls' (trip 4829149, on-time fix half-way 499→875 m (trip time 90 s), aged 10 s at fetch; framesAt sampled every 1 s with no new poll: distance strictly increases every second for 60 s — the clamp at fetchedAt + 90 s lets it reach 1200 m at fetchedAt + 80 s; today it freezes mid-track 20 s past 875 m) · 'the projection runs until 30 s after the next poll was due' (Transitland, a rail leg whose next stop the timetable reaches at fetchedAt + 89.5 s and the following one at fetchedAt + 150 s: still advancing at fetchedAt + 89 s, within 1 m of that stop from fetchedAt + 90 s on, and not past it at fetchedAt + 120 s — a shorter clamp stops it early, a longer one carries it on; today it coasts 20 s past the stop) · 'a projection that runs out holds at a station' (trip 4829149, on-time fix AT 499 m (trip time 60 s), aged 10 s: the timetable reaches 875 m at fetchedAt + 50 s and 1200 m only after the clamp, so from fetchedAt + 50 s through fetchedAt + 120 s the marker is within 1 m of 875 m — held AT the station, never mid-track; today frozen near 624 m).
§2 TELEPORT (gate 2). Root causes: reconcileLive.ts:86-91 jumps to the new target in one tick (≥ 50 m snaps); vehicleFrames.ts:123 discards the shown position when the matched trip changes (plan rebuilt every 15 s; Inner Loop car 51 jumped 189 m). FIX: ease corrections under 500 m over ~1 s by frame ticks (no AnimatedRegion — gate 4 re-checks m5c's frames_wired); snap only at ≥ 500 m; keep never-backward (a backward correction under 500 m holds); carry the position across a trip change by placing the shown point on the NEW trip's shape (placeOnShape with the timetable hint) instead of null. Gate 2 phrases: 'a 150 m correction eases in under 1.25 s' (marker at X, new fix → X+150 m: the first 250 ms tick moves < 150 m and the marker is within 1 m of the target by 1.25 s) · 'a correction of 500 m or more snaps' (a GUARD, like the 136 s case in §4: it already passes on today's ≥ 50 m snap; it keeps the new easing from swallowing real jumps) · 'a 200 m backward correction holds the marker' (marker at X, a new fix projecting to X − 200 m: no tick moves it backward; it holds at X until the new projection passes X, then moves on with it — today it snaps 200 m back) ·'a trip change carries the marker without a jump' (old trip's marker ran 150 m ahead of where the new plan's fix projects on the next trip: the first frame on the new trip is within 10 m of the last frame on the old one).
§3 LANES (gates 5, 6). Root cause: lane offsets are applied only to drawn lines (lineLayout.ts:144); markers use the unshifted track (vehicleFrames.ts:141,158; positions.ts:234; VehicleMarker.tsx:40) — G and O at one place are 0.0 m apart, each halfway between the two drawn lines. Gate 6 is an import-graph check (TypeScript AST, value imports only): markerLanes.ts's value-import closure holds src/ui/map/lineLayout.ts, and the Map route's (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx) closure holds markerLanes.ts — an `import type` or an importer the Map tab never mounts fails.
§4 "SOMETIMES LIVE" — THE ARBITER'S RELATIVE STALENESS RULE (gates 7–10, binding). Today vehicleVisual.ts:95 marks a marker stale when now − vehicle.timestamp > freshS 150 (constants.ts:24), the merge drops vehicles older than maxAgeS 210, and the pill (dataStatus.ts:83) judges the newest vehicle's age — but Transitland republishes its cached feed only ~every 2 min (header age at fetch 95 s / 121 s / 27 s), so most cycles every marker fades and some vanish while the pill says "Live". RULE: a VEHICLE is stale when it lags ITS OWN FEED — (feed header timestamp − vehicle timestamp) > 90 s; the FEED (pill) is "Live" while the header age (now − feedTimestamp) is ≤ 180 s, beyond that "Live · N min old" (minutesOld of the header age) AND every marker renders stale with it; DROP a vehicle only when its feed is older than 300 s OR it lags its feed by more than 300 s (replaces the absolute 210 s). Swiftly uses the same rule with lag 60 s, feed live 75 s, drop 150 s. PARSE TRAPS (gate 8 compares field for field against the raw body):
- Keep every itinerary and every leg, in order; never drop BUS legs.
- leg = {mode (the raw MOTIS string), routeShortName|null, headsign|null, from/to {name, stopId|null, epoch, latitude, longitude}, tripId|null, realTime, live: false, distanceM, durationS}.
- from.epoch = startTime and to.epoch = endTime, both in epoch seconds; durationS = duration.

- One request in flight: the same key shares the in-flight promise, and different keys queue.
- 60 s cache per (from, to, floor(timeEpoch/60), arriveBy), on the injected clock.
- Debounce: only the latest of a burst of calls fetches.
- One retry on 429/5xx, after a backoff on the injected sleep.
- Any failure → {kind: 'unavailable'}, never a throw: a second failure, a network rejection or a bad body. Standards accept a catch only if it contains throw or err(...), so wrap fetch in a Result helper.

Input never mutated; an itinerary no prediction touches is returned as the same object (m10a); an unpredicted leg is never marked live. milestones.title: Use Swiftly only on Wi-Fi: auto Wi-Fi detection (expo-network) gates Swiftly, with a Data & Settings switch, on by default
milestones.note:
WHY (Jamie, 2026-10-02 ~10:25, verbatim): "Can u build auto WiFi detection and have a setting in app that's like use swiftly only on wifi".
EVIDENCE: his 10:19 Data & Settings screenshot reads Swiftly "Live · updated 9 s ago · 475.5 KB per poll", "7 calls this month". "Per poll" is the mean over every Swiftly response (src/ui/settings/provider-health.ts:61). The Swiftly provider fetches the WHOLE-AGENCY gtfs-rt-trip-updates every 30 s while predictions are watched (src/live/providers/swiftly.ts). Transitland's copy of that feed measured 1,012,025 B on 2026-10-01. This crosses plan risk R19's 300 KB-per-poll line. On cellular, Transitland costs ~53 KB per vehicles poll (60 s) plus ~18 KB per station departures call.

MEASURED / READ (arbiter, 10:2x): SDK 57 docs (https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/network/, saved at .cache/expo-network-v57.html): expo-network is "Included in Expo Go", recommended ~57.0.2, NOT in package.json today; install with `npx expo install expo-network`. API: useNetworkState(), addNetworkStateListener(listener) -> EventSubscription, getNetworkStateAsync(). NetworkState = { type?, isConnected?, isInternetReachable? }. NetworkStateType on iOS: WIFI, CELLULAR, ETHERNET, NONE, UNKNOWN (VPN, OTHER, BLUETOOTH, WIMAX are Android-only); isConnected is false for NONE and UNKNOWN. The provider chain resolves PER CAPABILITY and skips a provider with no key (src/domain/live/chain.ts); it fails over after 3 failures and re-probes after 300 s.

ARBITER RULINGS (binding):
- Scope is literal: "use Swiftly only on Wi-Fi". With the setting ON and the phone NOT on Wi-Fi, Swiftly makes NO requests at all (neither vehicles nor trip-updates) and Transitland serves both capabilities, exactly as if Swiftly had no key. With the setting OFF, behaviour is today's.
- Default ON. Jamie asked for it because of the data cost; he can turn it off.
- "On Wi-Fi" = type WIFI or ETHERNET. CELLULAR, NONE, UNKNOWN, any other value, and "no reading yet" all count as NOT Wi-Fi (conservative: an unknown network never spends cellular data on Swiftly).
- A gated Swiftly is not a failing Swiftly. Gating accrues no failure count and no backoff and must not trigger the 3-failure failover or the 300 s re-probe wait. Back on Wi-Fi, Swiftly serves again at the NEXT poll tick (within one cadence).
- A request already in flight when the gate closes may finish. No NEW Swiftly request starts while gated.

WHAT TO BUILD:
A. SETTING. New src/live/swiftly-wifi.ts, modelled on walking-pace.ts: ONE expo-sqlite/kv-store item, 'settings.swiftly-wifi-only'; export function readSwiftlyWifiOnly(store = Storage): boolean returns true when the item is empty or unreadable (any value saveSwiftlyWifiOnly would not have written); export function saveSwiftlyWifiOnly(value: boolean, store = Storage): Result<boolean, ...> returns ok(the value read back); export const DEFAULT_SWIFTLY_WIFI_ONLY = true. Nothing is written until the rider toggles.
B. DETECTION. ONE app-wide network watch on expo-network, owned by the live runtime: LiveDataProvider (src/live/live-context.tsx) or the LiveRuntime it starts. getNetworkStateAsync once on mount, plus addNetworkStateListener; the subscription is removed on unmount. Never useNetworkState. Every listener event is the latest reading, a typeless one too: an event with no type is "any other value" (not Wi-Fi) and replaces the reading before it. Outside tests exactly one file in src/ calls addNetworkStateListener( or useNetworkState(, it is under src/live/, no other non-test file calls getNetworkStateAsync(, no other non-test file imports expo-network for a value (an aliased or namespace import counts, and so does a require() / import() whose constant specifier folds to it, e.g. 'expo-' + 'network'; an `import type` is fine), every require() / import() in non-test src names its module with a constant string (Metro bundles no other kind), and no non-test file names the ExpoNetwork native module ('ExpoNetwork' / 'onNetworkStateChanged' as an identifier, a property such as NativeModulesProxy.ExpoNetwork, a string, or a constant concatenation such as 'Expo' + 'Network'; comments never count). Pure export function isOnWifi(state: { type?: string } | null): boolean in NEW src/domain/live/network-gate.ts: true for type 'WIFI' or 'ETHERNET' only. The domain stays pure: it takes the strings 'WIFI' / 'ETHERNET', never the expo enum (no expo / react / react-native / '@/' import, no NetworkStateType).
C. GATE. Pure export function swiftlyAllowed({ wifiOnly, onWifi }): boolean = !wifiOnly || onWifi, in network-gate.ts. The chain treats a not-allowed Swiftly exactly like a key-less Swiftly, for BOTH capabilities. It records no call (the quota/call counter does not move), no failure and no backoff. The gate is re-read at every poll tick (the setting from the kv-store, the latest network reading), so a network change or a toggle takes effect within one cadence; the poller already makes an idle task due at once when its serving provider changes. The Keychain still holds Swiftly's key: LiveState.hasKey / keyHints keep reporting it (the key row keeps "Saved ••••…" and Remove); the runtime publishes whether Swiftly is gated in its state for Data & Settings (field name is the builder's).
D. DATA & SETTINGS (src/ui/settings/LiveDataSection.tsx, provider-health.ts). In the Swiftly card (after its heading, before Transitland's): a Switch, testID 'swiftly-wifi-only', accessibilityLabel exactly "Use Swiftly only on Wi-Fi" plus a visible label Text exactly "Use Swiftly only on Wi-Fi"; its value is readSwiftlyWifiOnly(); toggling saves through saveSwiftlyWifiOnly and the live runtime picks the change up within one cadence. The footer is exactly: "Keys stay in this phone's Keychain. Swiftly serves first when it has a key (only on Wi-Fi, if that is on); Transitland otherwise." (plain apostrophe).
E. INSTALL. `npx expo install expo-network` (an SDK-pinned ~57.x.y in dependencies, never devDependencies; package-lock and node_modules at 57.x); `npx expo install --check` passes (the gate runs it with EXPO_OFFLINE=1). milestones.title: Every hurry verdict walks the routed street distance (Transitous one-to-many) when one is known; only an estimate is labelled estimated
milestones.note:
WHY (Jamie, 2026-10-02 09:12, two screenshots): "Also says chill pace for getting to fifth but estimated walk time from Google Maps would put me at 1 min after scheduled arrival". The Now bar read "Missed · next 9:22 · chill · Fifth Street" at 9:12. Google: walk 11 min, 0.5 mi, arrive 9:23.

MEASURED (arbiter, 2026-10-02): Jamie's 9:12 spot was ~494 m straight-line from Fifth Street (stop 805, 25.769165,-80.192248), measured off his screenshot against the GTFS Riverwalk–Fifth Street spacing (210 m = 223 px). The engine walked 494 × 1.3 / 1.35 = 476 s against a slack of 570 s, so it said CHILL. Transitous one-to-many from that spot (one request, 09:21:29): Fifth Street distance 789.5 m. The routed walk is 1.60 × the straight line, not 1.3 ×. At Jamie's pace 789.5 / 1.35 = 585 s > 570 → not CHILL. Google agrees (11 min). THIS LOCATION IS JAMIE'S AND MUST NEVER ENTER THE REPO. The committed fixture (from the PUBLIC stop Third Street 815, 09:24:52): routed/straight ratios 2.03, 2.08, 1.31, 1.63, 1.19. No single detour constant is right. Server limits (/api/v1/map/initial serverConfig): MOTIS v2.11.3, maxOneToManySize 128, maxDirectTimeLimit 21600. withDistance=true returns distance (metres).
DURATION IS A COST, NOT A WALK TIME: osr's foot profile (master, include/osr/routing/profiles/foot.h:389–397) computes duration = dist / 1.2 m/s but cost = dist/(1.2 ± street adjustments) + 90 (non-foot way) + 45 (way with a separate sidewalk), + 90 per elevator node. Fixture Riverwalk: 292.7 m with "duration" 519 s (0.56 m/s): only a cost explains that (inferred from master; not checked against the v2.11.3 tag). So the verdict walks `distance` at the rider's pace, the same rule as mfix8's chip (WALK-leg distanceM / walkMps, no detour). Parse the field as costS so nobody later mistakes it for a time.

A. PURE CLIENT src/domain/walk/one-to-many.ts. Exports WALK_ROUTER_URL = 'https://api.transitous.org/api/v1/one-to-many', WALK_MAX_TARGETS = 128, WALK_MAX_S = 3600, WALK_MATCH_M = 250.
- buildWalkRequest(from: LatLon, targets: readonly LatLon[], appVersion: string) → Result<{url, headers}>. Query exactly one=<lat>;<lon>&many=<lat>;<lon>,...&mode=WALK&max=3600&maxMatchingDistance=250&arriveBy=false&withDistance=true, written literally with JS number formatting (never percent-encoded, like m10a's /plan URL). Headers exactly { 'User-Agent': … }: m10a's exact User-Agent, IMPORTED, not re-typed. m10a has no UA constant today (buildPlanRequest builds `MiamiTransit/${appVersion} (+${APP_REPO_URL})` inline), so src/domain/routes/transitous.ts gains export function transitousUserAgent(appVersion) and buildPlanRequest uses it too (m10a's exact-UA gates keep it honest). The pure domain has no expo-constants, so appVersion is a parameter: the provider passes src/ui/routes/plan-client.ts appVersion(). one-to-many.ts imports transitousUserAgent from '../routes/transitous' and contains no 'MiamiTransit' / 'purpleperkel'. Err when: 0 targets, > 128 targets, or a non-finite coordinate. Never throws.
- parseWalkTimes(json: unknown, n: number) → Result<readonly (WalkPath | null)[]>, WalkPath = {distanceM, costS}. The array must have length n. {} → null (no path). A finite, non-negative `distance` AND `duration` → a WalkPath {distanceM: distance, costS: duration}. A `duration` without a `distance`, or anything else (a distance without a duration, negative, non-number, null entry, non-array body) → Err. Never throws.

B. PURE POLICY src/domain/walk/walk-cache.ts. Exports REFRESH_MOVE_M = 150, MIN_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60, BACKOFF_MAX_S = 600, STALE_ORIGIN_M = 300; types WalkCache = { origin: LatLon; requestedAtS: number; paths: ReadonlyMap<string /* GTFS stop_id */, WalkPath | null> } (a key holding null is an entry with no path), WalkStop = { stopId, latitude, longitude } (a Platform fits), WalkEstimate = { walkMeters, detour, source: 'routed' | 'estimated' }.
- needsWalkRequest(cache, position, nowS, wantedStopIds, backoffUntilS): false while nowS < backoffUntilS, or while < 60 s have passed since the cache's request (requestedAtS); otherwise true if there is no cache, the rider is > 150 m (strict) from the cache origin, or a wanted stop has no entry (!paths.has(stopId)).
- walkFor(cache, stop, position) → {walkMeters, detour, source}. ROUTED when the entry has a path and the rider is <= 300 m from the cache origin: walkMeters = distanceM × straightNow / straightAtOrigin (just distanceM when straightAtOrigin < 50 m, so never a division by zero), detour 1. ESTIMATED otherwise (no cache, no entry, a null path, or > 300 m): the straight line rider → stop, detour = m7c's default 1.3 = HURRY_DEFAULTS.detour IMPORTED from '../hurry/verdict' (no 1.3 literal in walk-cache.ts code).

C. RUNTIME src/ui/walk/RoutedWalkProvider.tsx. ONE app-wide provider, mounted in src/app/_layout.tsx INSIDE UserLocationProvider and around the root Stack. It is the ONLY place in src/ (outside src/domain/walk and tests) that references buildWalkRequest or WALK_ROUTER_URL, and the endpoint literal is written only in one-to-many.ts (grep gate). Exports RoutedWalkProvider({ children, fetchWalk? }), type WalkFetch = (request: { url, headers }, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<Result<unknown /* the parsed JSON body */, LiveError>>, and useWalkTo(stops: readonly WalkStop[]): (stopId: string) => WalkEstimate.
- fetchWalk is an injectable prop. It defaults to the app's typed HTTP (the provider imports src/live/http.ts: abort timer, typed LiveErrors 'http' with its status / 'network' / 'timeout'), so tests never touch the network. Per PINNED RULE 2 the default is http.ts's EXPO_FETCH, wrapped by the provider (http.ts's httpGet is typed to the realtime providers); the gate pins the EXPO_FETCH import.
- useWalkTo(stops) registers the wanted stops (the union over every mounted consumer) and returns (stopId) => WalkEstimate from the rider's current position (walkFor over the provider's cache). WITHOUT A PROVIDER, useWalkTo returns the estimated fallback (walkFor(null, …)) and does not throw. This deliberately differs from UserLocationProvider, so that mfix8's and m7c's tests stay green unchanged. A gate pins that the root layout mounts the provider.
- The provider's clock is the wall clock (Date.now; the oracles' fake timers drive it).
- REQUEST RULES: only while AppState is 'active' (follow its 'change' events), and only with a position and >= 1 wanted stop; one request in flight; all wanted stops batched in one request (beyond 128, the nearest 128 to the rider; needsWalkRequest is asked about those 128, so farther stops never re-trigger a request every 60 s); obeys needsWalkRequest and re-checks ON ITS OWN when the 60 s gap or a backoff ends (a pending move is asked for without a new fix); the request is made from the rider's position (one=) and its answer becomes the cache with that origin and the request's time; on 429, 5xx, network or timeout — and, by this card's choice, any other failure (another status, an unparseable body) — back off 60 → 120 → 240 → 480 → 600 s and keep the old cache; a success resets the backoff.

D. WIRING. Then every verdict in the app walks a routed distance when one is known.
- The Now bar's near-trip verdict (mfix8's path): walk the ride's boarding platform via walkFor (useWalkTo in src/ui/now, through useNearTripWalk in src/ui/now/near-trip-walk.ts: PINNED RULE 5).
- The station sheet's verdicts (useStationHurryVerdict / StationHurry): same, per direction's platform (useWalkTo in src/ui/hurry).
- The route chip keeps mfix8's routed plan legs while the rider is within mfix8's CHIP_ROUTED_START_M (50 m, arbiter ruling 09:3x after the mfix8 prover) of the itinerary's start. OFF THE START (> 50 m), mfix8 falls back to mfix5's straight line from the rider; mfix9 replaces that fallback with walkFor to the first ride's boarding platform: src/ui/routes/route-options.ts OptionContext gains walk?: (stopId: string) => WalkEstimate (stopId = gtfsStopId of the first ride's from.stopId); off the start routeOptions judges the first ride with hurryVerdict over the estimate's walkMeters and detour; without walk it stays mfix5's straight line × 1.3 (mfix5's spies stay green); the plan screen passes useWalkTo over the itineraries' first-ride boarding stops (useWalkTo in src/ui/routes).
- ARBITER RULING F2 (lands in mfix8's fix round, 2026-10-02): useChipPosition follows the rider for EVERY plan (position = rider.coordinate ?? start), not only for "Route from here". So for a plan from the rider's own location (its start is the ONE fix taken when the sheet opened), a rider more than 50 m off the start walks via walkFor too. PlanScreen therefore registers the first rides' boarding stops (useWalkTo) for EVERY plan while the rider has a fix, not only for "Route from here" (no fix, no stops). The chip_screen oracle drives the REAL PlanScreen under the provider twice: "Route from here" with the rider 400 m off the start, then a plan from the rider's own location (the one fix at the fixture's START) with the rider 300 m off its start. Each time: exactly 1 one-to-many request, from the rider (for the location plan: exactly the first rides' boarding stops); fed, the chips walk the routed walk (for the location plan: every chip differs from the estimate); with {} for every target, the chips are the no-provider estimate. Every sheet opens at the fixture's query time, so chips are compared at one instant.

E. COPY. The visible text stays "~N min walk" with N = ceil(walkS / 60). The bar's VoiceOver label says "estimated" ONLY when the source is 'estimated'. When routed it never says "estimated", and it carries the exact phrase "walk along streets" (case-insensitive).

F. ORACLE ON THE COMMITTED FIXTURE, rider at stop 815, Fifth Street platform 805, Jamie's default paces 1.35 / 2.7 (recomputed with the repo's haversine, src/lib/geo.ts, R = 6371008.8 m): straight line 342.03 m → estimated walkS 329.36 s (the brief's ≈ 329.3). Routed 710.64 m → walkS 526.40 s, jogS 263.20 s. One departure at now + 30 + 400 s (slack 400): estimated says CHILL, routed says JOG (no later departure). That is Jamie's bug in public data; the bar and the station sheet must both show the routed verdict when the provider is fed the fixture. On the real schedule (the Mover every 300 s) the bar and sheet oracles take T = 430 s before Wednesday 2026-09-30's first Fifth Street → Bayfront Park ride from platform 805 (05:34:00, so T = 05:26:50, slack 400): the saved trip Fifth Street → Bayfront Park reads (at REGULAR_LINE_MAX_CHARS 38) ["Bayfront Park", "Chill · 1 min spare · ~6 min walk"] estimated and ["Bayfront Park", "Not worth it · ~9 min walk"] routed (the 05:39 train follows within 360 s); every Fifth Street sheet card goes from "Chill, a walk makes the 5:34 train with 1 minute to spare, …" to "Not worth hurrying for the 5:34 train, another leaves in 12 minutes, …" (PINNED RULE 3). 300 s earlier (700 s of slack) every card is CHILL with the spare the routed 710.6 m leaves, which differs from the spare of the estimate, of a fixed 1.6 detour and of the routing cost read as metres. The oracles compute these with the shipped engine.

G. REQUEST DISCIPLINE (fake fetch; fake timers stepped in <= 1 s increments inside act, per the repo's act() trap; positions stepped through the real UserLocationProvider's one watch):
- no fix → no request; the first fix with wanted stops → exactly 1 (within 2 s), from the rider's position, carrying every wanted stop and m10a's User-Agent;
- moving <= 150 m → none;
- > 150 m and >= 60 s → 1;
- > 150 m inside 60 s → none until 60 s, then 1 (by 76 s);
- a pending request plus another trigger (new fixes, a new consumer's stop) → still 1 call;
- backgrounded → none; foregrounded → 1 (within 16 s);
- two consumers → ONE request with the union; 130 wanted stops → one request with the nearest 128;
- 429 → the next attempt waits >= 60 s (comes by 76 s), then >= 120 s (by 136 s); a success resets it (503 → 60 s); a network failure → 120 s;
- after a failure, routed values hold (scaled from the kept cache) while <= 300 m from the origin, then fall back to estimated.

H. HYGIENE. The fixture lands at src/domain/walk/__fixtures__/transitous-one-to-many.json with this card's commit (the ARBITER commits it; never re-capture, never commit a rider's position). A gate checks that its origin is stop 815's GTFS coordinates in assets/db/schedule.db, each target is the GTFS stop it names at its DB coordinates, _provenance names Transitous and ODbL, each answer is {} or exactly {duration, distance}, and there is no key or geometry field. Only labelled native mocks (mocks_native_only over the walk, now, hurry and routes __tests__ dirs): fetchWalk is injected, never mocked; AppState is set on react-native's own jest mock. The 3 pure oracles (tsx: client, cache, fixture) and 9 jest oracles (fallback, requests, batch, backoff, default_fetch, bar, sheet, chip, chip_screen) check the SHIPPED modules by the exact paths and names in the verify header's BINDING CONTRACT, independently of these tests; run one alone: bash -c 'source "$0"; mfix9_oracle requests' scripts/ratchet/verify-mfix9_routed_walk.sh

ONE FUNCTION decides a saved trip's walk: src/ui/trips/trip-walk.ts export function savedTripWalk(trip: Pick<SavedTrip, 'start' | 'walkOverrideMin'>, input: SavedTripWalkInput): SavedTripWalk | null. SavedTripWalkInput = { platforms: readonly WalkStop[] (the trip's boarding platforms: the platforms its rides over TRIP_HORIZON_S from now board at, else the origin's platforms, which is trip-verdict.ts:70-72's rule); position: LatLon | null (the rider's); walkMps: number (REQUIRED: readWalkingPace().walkMps from the caller; it throws (invariant) when it is missing, 0, NaN or negative; it never supplies a default); walk?: (stopId) => WalkEstimate (mfix9's useWalkTo over those platforms, which walks from the RIDER) }. SavedTripWalk = { source: 'override' | 'routed' | 'estimated'; from: 'setting' | 'here' | 'start'; walkS; minutes; stopId: string | null }. Precedence:
1. the trip's walkOverrideMin (Jamie's explicit setting) -> source 'override', from 'setting', walkS = minutes x 60, minutes = the override (0 stays 0), stopId null. It needs no position, and it beats a known routed walk.
2. otherwise the walk starts at the rider's position; with no position, at the trip's saved start; with neither, null (no walk is known: the card says so, and the countdown runs to the buffer alone, as m7b does today). The platform is the input platform NEAREST that origin (straight line; a tie keeps the first listed), and only that platform's walk is asked for.
3. 'routed' (from 'here'): the walk starts at the rider and walk(stopId).source is 'routed'. walkS = Math.ceil(walkMeters x detour / walkMps).
4. otherwise 'estimated' (from 'here', or 'start' when there is no position): walkS = Math.ceil(the straight line to that platform x HURRY_DEFAULTS.detour (1.3, imported) / walkMps).
walkS is whole seconds rounded UP (a walk is never underestimated, and ceil(ceil(x) / 60) = ceil(x / 60), so the card's minutes always equal the bar's for the same metres). minutes = Math.ceil(walkS / 60) is what EVERY screen shows.
